name: Teriparatide
summary: Anabolic bone drug that increases bone formation.
lead: Teriparatide is a recombinant form of the first 34 amino acids of human parathyroid hormone (PTH 1-34), the portion that activates the PTH1 receptor . It is a prescription bone-anabolic drug given by daily subcutaneous injection to treat osteoporosis, and was first marketed by Eli Lilly as Forteo . Unlike most osteoporosis drugs, which slow bone breakdown, it stimulates new bone formation .
claims: Bone-forming drugs like teriparatide can thicken bones
Teriparatide has no meaningful side effects

name: Romosozumab
summary: Sclerostin-blocking antibody that builds bone and slows resorption.
lead: Romosozumab, sold as Evenity, is a humanized monoclonal antibody that binds and inhibits sclerostin, a protein made by bone-embedded osteocytes that restrains bone formation . It is a prescription medicine given by subcutaneous injection to treat osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk of fracture, and the US label limits use to 12 monthly doses, after which an antiresorptive drug is advised if therapy remains warranted . It was approved in Japan in January 2019, the United States in April 2019 and the European Union in December 2019, and the FDA regards it as a first-in-class medication .

name: Vitamin K2
summary: Cofactor for bone-mineralization proteins. Supplement trial data mixed.
lead: Vitamin K2, or menaquinone (MK), is one of the forms of vitamin K, alongside K1 (phylloquinone) and the synthetic K3 (menadione). It is a family of fat-soluble compounds named MK-4 to MK-13 for the length of their isoprenoid side chain, with MK-4 and MK-7 the forms most often sold as supplements . MK-4 is found in animal products and is made in animal tissues from K1, while longer-chain forms such as MK-7 occur in fermented foods, notably the Japanese soybean dish natto, and some cheeses .
claims: Megadosing K2 (MK-4 or MK-7) builds new bone and improves facial structure
Vitamin K2 acts like a hormone by activating the SXR receptor and many genes
Calcium, D3 and K2 together maximise height growth
K2 supplementation produces noticeable personal effects, and stopping it causes problems

name: Calcium
summary: Necessary for bone mineralization.
lead: Calcium (symbol Ca, atomic number 20) is an alkaline earth metal that is the most abundant metal in the human body and an essential mineral . More than 99 percent of body calcium is stored in the skeleton, mostly as hydroxyapatite, where it provides rigidity and acts as a reservoir; the remaining 1 percent in blood and tissues is involved in blood clotting, muscle contraction, nerve transmission, hormone secretion and enzyme activation . Dietary calcium comes from dairy products, fortified foods, some leafy greens and supplements.
claims: Adequate calcium is needed to gain bone mass or density
Calcium supplements increase heart attack risk, so food sources are preferable
Milk has estrogenic effects and can lower testosterone
Eggshells are a free source of calcium

name: Magnesium
summary: Required for normal skeletal and neuromuscular physiology.
lead: Magnesium (symbol Mg, atomic number 12) is an alkaline earth metal and an essential mineral that is required for about 300 enzymes in the human body and interacts with ATP, DNA and RNA . Roughly half of the body's magnesium is held in bone, according to clinical summaries. It supports nerve and muscle function, energy production, blood pressure and glucose regulation, and is obtained from nuts, seeds, legumes, leafy greens and some fruit juices . Magnesium compounds are also used medicinally as laxatives and antacids and to treat eclampsia .
claims: Magnesium glycinate with L-theanine and GABA improves sleep, to the point of sleeping very late
Magnesium oil promotes hair growth or reduces hair loss
Magnesium can cure benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV)

name: Boron
summary: Trace element studied for mineral and hormone metabolism.
lead: Boron (symbol B, atomic number 5) is a metalloid element that occurs in nature combined with oxygen in borate minerals and is essential to plant cell-wall formation . For people, boron is a trace element found in fruit, vegetables, nuts and legumes, and it is sold as a supplement typically as boric acid, calcium fructoborate or boron citrate. It is generally not classed as an essential human nutrient, although it is considered by some authors to be beneficial, and the US Dietary Reference Intakes report of 2001 addressed it among trace elements .
claims: Boron raises free testosterone and lowers SHBG
Most people are boron deficient, so supplementing is a sensible default
Boron-rich foods such as raisins and pomegranate juice can serve as a boron source
Boron helps joint and bone health

name: BPC-157
summary: The internet-famous healing peptide — tendon, gut, wound-repair claims. Almost entirely animal data.
lead: BPC-157 (Body Protection Compound 157, also called bepecin or PL 14736) is a synthetic peptide of fifteen amino acids whose sequence is derived from a protein found in human gastric juice. It was first described by the pharmacologist Predrag Sikiric and colleagues at the University of Zagreb in the early 1990s, and nearly all of the published research on it comes from animal experiments, a large share of them from that group .
claims: BPC-157 heals tendon and muscle injuries much faster than normal.
BPC-157 and TB-500 work synergistically as a 'recovery stack'.
It is safe because there are almost no reported side effects.
BPC-157 helps with other problems such as tinnitus or gut conditions.

name: TB-500
summary: Tissue-repair and cell-migration pathways. Preclinical; product identity varies.
lead: TB-500 is the name used by research-peptide suppliers for a synthetic version of thymosin beta-4 (Tβ4), a small protein found in most human cells, or for a fragment of it. Analytical chemistry work on a veterinary product called TB-500 found its key ingredient to be a short, N-terminally acetylated fragment of Tβ4 covering residues 17 to 23 (Ac-LKKTETQ), the region associated with actin binding, rather than the full-length protein . Because the term is used loosely, what a given vendor sells under the name can differ.
claims: TB-500 speeds healing of muscle and tendon injuries.
TB-500 and BPC-157 together are a more effective healing stack.
TB-500 may improve skin or wrinkles and general anti-ageing.
TB-500 carries risks, including tumour growth, that outweigh benefits.

name: KPV
summary: α-MSH-derived anti-inflammatory tripeptide. Preclinical.
lead: KPV is a tripeptide made of lysine, proline and valine (Lys-Pro-Val). It corresponds to the C-terminal end (residues 11 to 13) of alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (alpha-MSH), a peptide that regulates pigmentation and also influences inflammation . KPV is the portion of the hormone that retains anti-inflammatory activity but lacks the sequence motif associated with pigment and other melanocortin-receptor effects .
claims: KPV reduces inflammation and aids recovery from soft-tissue injuries.
KPV is a gut-healing peptide that helps with bowel inflammation.
KPV gives the benefits of alpha-MSH without pigmentation or other hormone effects.
Adding KPV to a BPC-157 and TB-500 stack is synergistic.

name: Thymosin alpha-1
summary: Immune-modulating peptide with real human research — for medical conditions, not looks.
lead: Thymosin alpha-1 (Tα1) is a 28-amino-acid peptide, N-terminally acetylated, produced by cleavage of a longer precursor called prothymosin alpha. It was the first peptide from the calf-thymus preparation known as thymosin fraction 5 to be completely sequenced and synthesised . Its synthetic form is known as thymalfasin and has been sold under the brand name Zadaxin; Wikipedia states it is approved in some countries for hepatitis B and C and is used to boost immune responses in other diseases .
claims: Thymosin alpha-1 optimises or boosts the immune system in healthy people.
Thymosin alpha-1 helps with chronic viral infections such as hepatitis B.
It reduces mortality in severe infections such as sepsis or COVID-19.
Thymosin alpha-1 improves appearance or slows visible ageing.

name: Curcumin
summary: Anti-inflammatory polyphenol. Absorption is poor without piperine or special forms.
lead: Curcumin is the principal curcuminoid, a yellow polyphenol pigment, of turmeric (Curcuma longa), a member of the ginger family. It is sold as a dietary supplement and cosmetic ingredient, used as a food flavouring and colouring (E100 in the European Union), and has a long history in traditional medicine .
claims: Curcumin reduces joint pain and inflammation.
Micellar or 'third-generation' curcumin is about 95 times better absorbed, so older research understates it.
Curcumin speeds recovery from exercise and soreness.
Curcumin benefits skin and appearance.

name: N-Acetylcysteine
summary: Glutathione precursor with established medical uses.
lead: N-acetylcysteine (NAC, acetylcysteine) is the N-acetyl derivative of the amino acid L-cysteine. It is an established medicine, used as the antidote for paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose and as a mucolytic that loosens thick mucus in chronic lung disease, and it is on the World Health Organization's List of Essential Medicines. It is also widely sold as a dietary supplement .
claims: NAC protects the liver while using testosterone or oral steroids.
NAC raises glutathione and works as a general antioxidant.
NAC helps depression, compulsions and sleep by lowering glutamate.
NAC supports exercise recovery and performance.

name: Glycine
summary: Collagen's main building block. Cheap, safe, also helps sleep.
lead: Glycine (Gly, G) is the simplest stable amino acid, with a single hydrogen atom as its side chain, and the only common amino acid that is not chiral. It is a building block of proteins and makes up about 35 percent of the amino acid content of collagen, where its small size allows the tight coiling of the triple helix . It is classed as non-essential because the body synthesises it, though Wikipedia notes it is considered semi-essential because the amount made may not meet all metabolic needs .
claims: Glycine improves hair, nails and skin because it is needed for collagen synthesis
Glycine can replace dietary sugar because it tastes sweet
Glycine adds a small increase in looks rating (0.05 to 0.2 PSL)
Glycine is better taken as collagen powder because amino acids compete for absorption

name: Taurine
summary: Cell-protective amino acid; thin evidence for appearance outcomes.
lead: Taurine (2-aminoethanesulfonic acid) is a naturally occurring sulfur-containing compound found in high concentrations in muscle, heart, retina and brain. Chemically it is an amino sulfonic acid rather than a carboxylic amino acid, and because it is not incorporated into proteins it is classed as non-proteinogenic, though it is usually still called an amino acid . It is made in the human liver from cysteine and methionine, and is also obtained from meat and fish .
claims: Taurine improves workouts and endurance.
Taurine calms the nervous system and helps sleep after hard training.
Taurine prevents muscle cramps.
Large daily doses protect the heart and body during steroid use.

name: Boswellia serrata
summary: Botanical studied for inflammation and joint symptoms.
lead: Boswellia serrata is a tree native to India and neighbouring parts of the Indian subcontinent whose gum resin, known as Indian frankincense, has long been used in Ayurvedic medicine . The resin contains pentacyclic triterpenoids called boswellic acids, including beta-boswellic acid and acetyl-11-keto-beta-boswellic acid (AKBA), which are the compounds most often used to standardise commercial extracts .
claims: Boswellia eases arthritic and sore joints
It works as a natural 5-LOX inhibitor and so controls inflammation
Stacking it with curcumin, bromelain, fish oil and glucosamine amplifies recovery
Boswellia has benefits for appearance or physique

name: Bromelain
summary: Pineapple enzyme studied for swelling and inflammation. Mixed.
lead: Bromelain is an extract from pineapple, mainly the stem, containing a mixture of protein-digesting enzymes and smaller amounts of other compounds . The best-known enzymes are stem bromelain and fruit bromelain, both sulfhydryl (cysteine) proteases . It is used industrially as a meat tenderiser and in baking and cosmetics manufacturing, and is sold as an oral supplement, often aimed at swelling, bruising and general inflammation .
claims: Bromelain reduces swelling and bruising after injury or surgery
Eating pineapple provides the same benefits as the supplement
It acts as a digestive enzyme that helps with large food intake
Bromelain can thin the blood and cause bleeding with antiplatelet drugs

name: NMN
summary: NAD+ precursor. The biochemistry is real; visible rejuvenation is unproven.
lead: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is a biosynthetic intermediate in the production of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD+), a coenzyme involved in redox reactions and a substrate for signalling enzymes such as sirtuins and PARPs . In the body it is made from nicotinamide by the enzyme NAMPT, or from nicotinamide riboside by nicotinamide riboside kinases, and is converted to NAD+ by NMNAT enzymes . It is sold as an oral supplement and, in some products, as a topical skincare ingredient .
claims: NMN restores NAD+ and slows or reverses ageing
NMN rejuvenates arteries and circulation
NMN could heal intestinal damage in inflammatory bowel disease
NMN improves physical performance

name: Nicotinamide riboside
summary: NAD+ precursor with human biochemical evidence; longevity unproven.
lead: Nicotinamide riboside (NR) is a pyridine-nucleoside and a form of vitamin B3 that serves as a precursor to the coenzyme NAD+ . Inside cells it is phosphorylated by nicotinamide riboside kinases (NRK1 and NRK2) to nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), which is then converted to NAD+ by NMNAT enzymes, bypassing other known NAD+ synthesis routes . It is sold as an oral supplement under brands such as Tru Niagen and is closely related to, and often compared with, NMN .
claims: NR gives noticeable energy
NR slows ageing by restoring NAD+
NR is safe for long-term stacking with resveratrol and other supplements

name: Resveratrol
summary: Polyphenol studied for sirtuin signaling. Human longevity evidence insufficient.
lead: Resveratrol (3,5,4'-trihydroxy-trans-stilbene) is a polyphenol of the stilbenoid class produced by plants such as grapes, blueberries, raspberries, mulberries and peanuts in response to injury or pathogens . Most US supplements are derived from the root of Japanese knotweed . It is sold as an oral supplement and is an ingredient in some skincare products, and it became widely known through laboratory reports that it activates sirtuins and extends lifespan in some organisms .
claims: Resveratrol is a powerful natural aromatase inhibitor that lowers estrogen
Resveratrol slows ageing and extends lifespan
It protects against heart disease and insulin resistance
It counters endocrine-disrupting chemicals and inflammation

name: Spermidine
summary: Autophagy-linked polyamine. Preliminary human data.
lead: Spermidine is a naturally occurring polyamine (C7H19N3) found in all living cells, first isolated from semen, and present in foods such as wheat germ, soybeans, mushrooms and aged cheese . It is a precursor to spermine and takes part in cell growth, membrane function and RNA and DNA stabilisation . It is sold as an oral supplement, often as wheat germ extract, and is promoted as an autophagy-inducing longevity compound .
claims: Spermidine extends lifespan by inducing autophagy
Eating wheat germ or other spermidine-rich foods is a practical way to get the benefit
Spermidine improves memory and brain health
Spermidine promotes hair growth

name: Urolithin A
summary: Mitophagy booster with early human trials (muscle endurance).
lead: Urolithin A is a benzocoumarin compound formed when gut bacteria transform ellagic acid and ellagitannins, polyphenols found in pomegranates, walnuts, raspberries, strawberries and oak-aged wine . It is not known to occur in any food itself, and how much a person produces depends on their gut microbiota, with efficiency varying widely and some individuals showing no conversion . Supplements providing urolithin A directly are marketed for muscle and mitochondrial health in ageing, the best known being a branded form called Mitopure .
claims: Urolithin A repairs mitochondria and improves muscle
Pomegranate or ellagitannin foods give the same benefit
It improves sexual health and brain function

name: Coenzyme Q10
summary: Electron-transport cofactor. Established physiology; limited cosmetic evidence.
lead: Coenzyme Q10 (CoQ10, ubiquinone, ubidecarenone) is a lipid-soluble benzoquinone made by the human body and found in meat, fish, seed oils and some vegetables . It is a cofactor in the mitochondrial electron transport chain, where it supports ATP production, and it also acts as a membrane antioxidant . The body synthesises it through a pathway that shares an early step with cholesterol, via HMG-CoA reductase, which is why statin drugs have been proposed to lower CoQ10 levels .
claims: Statins deplete CoQ10, so users should take it with them
CoQ10 supports heart health
Topical CoQ10 reduces wrinkles and slows skin ageing
It provides mitochondrial energy support for fatigue and ageing

name: Alpha-lipoic acid
summary: Redox cofactor and antioxidant. Thin appearance evidence.
lead: Alpha-lipoic acid (ALA), also called lipoic acid or thioctic acid, is an organosulfur compound derived from octanoic acid. It is made in small amounts by the body and serves as an essential cofactor for several mitochondrial enzyme complexes involved in aerobic energy metabolism. It is also sold as an over-the-counter dietary supplement in the United States and as a drug in some countries, where it is marketed as an antioxidant and for glucose metabolism.
claims: The R-form is the only version worth taking; the racemic form is "useless"
ALA improves insulin sensitivity and helps with carb handling
ALA helps damaged nerves regenerate
ALA is a powerful antioxidant that works by scavenging free radicals

name: Fisetin
summary: Flavonoid senolytic candidate. Preclinical.
lead: Fisetin (3,3',4',7-tetrahydroxyflavone) is a plant flavonol in the polyphenol family. It occurs as a yellow pigment in fruits and vegetables such as strawberries, apples, persimmons, onions and cucumbers, and its chemical formula was first described by the Austrian chemist Josef Herzig in 1891. It is sold as an over-the-counter dietary supplement and is discussed in longevity communities as a candidate senolytic, a compound proposed to selectively clear senescent cells.
claims: Fisetin clears senescent cells and extends lifespan
Fisetin supports mitochondrial repair and healthy ageing
Fisetin reduces body fat, regulates blood sugar and protects skin from UV
Dietary fisetin from strawberries is beneficial

name: Quercetin
summary: Antioxidant flavonoid with investigational senolytic effects.
lead: Quercetin is a plant flavonol in the polyphenol group of flavonoids. It occurs in many fruits, vegetables, leaves, seeds and grains, with capers, red onions and kale among the foods containing appreciable amounts, and it is used as an ingredient in dietary supplements, beverages and foods. The name has been used since 1857 and derives from the Latin for oak forest, after the genus Quercus. Average dietary intake is estimated at 25 to 50 mg per day.
claims: Quercetin is a senolytic that clears senescent cells
Quercetin helps with COVID and long-COVID fatigue
Quercetin is an anti-inflammatory antioxidant that protects health
Quercetin affects hormones or iodine status

name: Rapamycin
summary: mTOR inhibitor at the center of aging research. Human longevity unproven.
lead: Rapamycin, also called sirolimus and sold under the brand name Rapamune among others, is a macrolide compound produced by the soil bacterium Streptomyces hygroscopicus. It was first isolated in the early 1970s from a soil sample taken on Easter Island (Rapa Nui), which gave the compound its name. It was first studied as an antifungal, but its potent immunosuppressive and antiproliferative properties, which arise from inhibiting the kinase mTOR, redirected its development.
claims: Rapamycin slows ageing because it inhibits mTOR
Low-dose or intermittent rapamycin avoids the side effects seen in transplant patients
Rapamycin is too blunt an instrument for healthy people
Topical rapamycin can rejuvenate skin

name: Metformin
summary: Diabetes drug with AMPK-related metabolic effects. Longevity unproven.
lead: Metformin, sold under the brand name Glucophage among others, is a biguanide medication taken by mouth and the main first-line drug for type 2 diabetes, particularly in people who are overweight. It is also used in polycystic ovary syndrome (which Wikipedia terms polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome) and sometimes off-label to limit metabolic effects of antipsychotic drugs. It was first described in the scientific literature in 1922 by Emil Werner and James Bell, studied in humans by the French physician Jean Sterne in the 1950s, and introduced as a medication in France in 1957. It is on the WHO List of Essential Medicines and in 2023 was the third most commonly prescribed medication in
claims: Metformin slows ageing and extends lifespan
Metformin helps with belly fat and carbohydrate sensitivity
Metformin inhibits muscle growth
Metformin from overseas pharmacies is a way to manage blood sugar during hormone use

name: Epitalon
summary: Telomere-hype peptide. No reliable human anti-aging evidence.
lead: Epitalon, also spelled epithalon or epithalone, is a synthetic tetrapeptide with the amino acid sequence alanine-glutamic acid-aspartic acid-glycine (Ala-Glu-Asp-Gly, AEDG) and the molecular formula C14H22N4O9. It was designed from the amino acid composition of epithalamin, an extract of bovine pineal gland, and has been described as the putative active component of that preparation. Most of the research on epitalon and epithalamin comes from the St. Petersburg Institute of Bioregulation and Gerontology, led by Vladimir Khavinson, although laboratories elsewhere have recently begun to study it.
claims: Epitalon lengthens telomeres and slows ageing
Epitalon extends human lifespan
Epitalon improves cognition and brain function
Epitalon is anti-cancer, or alternatively could promote cancer via telomerase

name: MOTS-c
summary: Mitochondria-derived peptide studied for metabolic signaling. Preclinical.
lead: MOTS-c (mitochondrial open reading frame of the 12S rRNA-c) is a 16-amino-acid peptide, with the sequence MRWQEMGYIFYPRKLR, encoded in humans by the mitochondrial MT-RNR1 gene. It belongs to the mitochondrial-derived peptides (MDPs), short peptides encoded by small open reading frames in mitochondrial DNA, of which eight have been identified. It is believed to take part in the regulation of glucose metabolism by skeletal muscle, rises with exercise, and is described as an exercise mimetic.
claims: MOTS-c is an exercise mimetic that burns fat
MOTS-c reverses age-related decline
MOTS-c complements GLP-1 drugs and growth hormone secretagogues in a stack
MOTS-c is a safe natural peptide because the body makes it

name: SS-31
summary: Mitochondria-targeted peptide in disease research. No proven cosmetic anti-aging.
lead: SS-31, also called elamipretide (brand name Forzinity), is a synthetic mitochondria-targeted tetrapeptide developed by Stealth BioTherapeutics. It binds cardiolipin, a phospholipid found on the inner mitochondrial membrane, and is given by subcutaneous injection as the hydrochloride salt. In September 2025 the US Food and Drug Administration granted it accelerated approval, as a first-in-class medicine, for improving muscle strength in people with Barth syndrome who weigh at least 30 kg; Barth syndrome is a rare, life-threatening mitochondrial disease that mostly affects males.
claims: SS-31 boosts mitochondrial energy and fights ageing
Vendor SS-31 is equivalent to the approved drug
SS-31 is effective for mitochondrial disease
SS-31 helps cosmetic skin anti-aging and wound healing
